signals.summary: Pilates-inspired boutique formats (STRONG Pilates and the ongoing 'Pilates princess' celebrity aesthetic) keep the reformer studio front-of-mind. Extremely producible: reformers, springs, socks, pastel studios and mirror-and-light interiors carry the whole look without a body.
signals.why_now: health.com STRONG Pilates explainer (~67h, one of the fresher fitness items) plus Glam 'bye-bye Pilates princess' celebrity-trend piece (~1029h) - a thin but genuinely two-source studio-format thread.

signals.summary: Hyrox (functional-fitness race format: sleds, ski-ergs, sandbags, wall balls, rowers in an arena circuit) keeps generating global coverage as it spreads across demographics and countries. Produce via the equipment stations and arena/gym environments, not racing bodies.
signals.why_now: 5+ independent outlets: DW (~196h), The Times / Chinese pensioners angle (~222h), ABC + Yahoo explainers (~342h), USA Today 'new CrossFit?' (~3318h) - sustained, recurring cross-market coverage rather than a single spike.

signals.summary: A broad 'move well as you age' wave: mobility drills, stretching debates, and hip/ankle mobility routines pitched for over-35/over-50 audiences. Producible through mats, resistance bands, foam rollers and studio floors in morning light, though the demo itself leans body-based.
signals.why_now: 7+ independent outlets recurring: health.com stretch-after-workout (~67h), Runner's World over-50 (~163h), Outside 'move younger' (~1854h), SELF 14 moves over 35 (~3726h), AP mobility-with-age (~5573h), Katie Couric, Kern Valley seniors - a persistent evergreen swell.

signals.summary: Cultural shift framing strength training - not calorie-burn or weight loss - as the primary gym goal. Producible via racks, barbells, dumbbells, chalk and empty weight-room environments as objects; skip the lifting body.
signals.why_now: Yahoo Creators 'strength training replacing weight loss as top goal' (~294h) plus a widely-shared squats-as-one-exercise blog (~116h) and the broader shift echoed in group-fitness 'health over calorie-burn' pieces - a stable multi-source theme.

signals.summary: Interest in recovery as a lifestyle ritual - saunas, cold plunge, foam rollers, dim recovery corners. Highly producible as objects and interiors (steam, ice, towels, wood-panelled sauna). Frame around the ritual space, avoiding any supplement/peptide efficacy claims.
signals.why_now: Medical Xpress 'biohacks or basics, what works in recovery' (~3342h) and RNZ burnout-recovery (~37h, fresh) anchor it, alongside outdoor-sauna and wearable-recovery chatter. Recovery framing recurs across several outlets.

signals.summary: A counter-trend celebrating minimal, gentle movement - 'Zone 0', walking, doing almost nothing. Producible via serene walking paths, parks, quiet studio corners and morning-light environments rather than exertion imagery.
signals.why_now: ELLE 'case for doing less' (~2358h), WSJ 'workout about doing almost nothing' (~3870h), NY Post 'Zone 0' (~5645h) and a 'forget cardio' group-fitness shift piece (~1902h) - four independent outlets on the same low-effort theme.

signals.summary: Community-driven group workouts and 'connection is the new exercise' framing across Gen Z and NYC scenes. Producible via full studio/class spaces, run-club meetups and shared equipment settings shown as environments, not individual faces.
signals.why_now: Steve Magness 'connection is the new exercise' (~24h, fresh, HN-surfaced), Medscape Gen Z group-workout piece, NY Post NYC group-fitness exclusive, plus a 'surprising group fitness shift' feature - four independent sources.
